parameters.content:
## START HERE

**1. Open the SETTINGS node** and fill in four things:

- **freshdesk_domain** - your subdomain, the part before .freshdesk.com
- **customgpt_agent_id** - the number in your agent URL
- **allowed_tags** - every tag the agent may use, comma separated. Nothing else gets written.
- **allowed_types** - your Freshdesk ticket Types, spelled exactly as Freshdesk spells them

Optional: **skip_senders** - email addresses your own alerting sends from. Leave blank to classify everything.

Do not switch the SETTINGS node to **JSON mode**. n8n discards the fields and switching back does not restore them. If that happens, re-import the template.

**2. Connect three credentials:**

- **Freshdesk account** on the four Freshdesk nodes - a Freshdesk API credential with your domain and API key
- **CustomGPT API Key** on Create Conversation and Ask Agent - a Header Auth credential with name `Authorization` and value `Bearer YOUR-CUSTOMGPT-KEY`
- **Freshdesk Webhook Secret** on the Webhook node - a Header Auth credential with name `X-Webhook-Secret`, holding the same secret you paste into the Freshdesk automation rule

A 401 tells you which one is wrong: on Get Ticket it is the Freshdesk key, on Create Conversation it is the CustomGPT key, on the webhook itself the secret does not match the Freshdesk rule.

**3. Test before going live.** Put a ticket number you do not mind changing into Test Ticket ID and click Execute Workflow. This writes to that ticket. You do not need the Freshdesk automation rule yet.

Preflight Check stops the run with a plain-English message if anything is missing.

## Reading the ticket

Skip Automated Senders only drops mail from addresses you listed in skip_senders. Leave that blank and everything gets classified - including noise, which is the point. Noise you have labelled is noise you can filter.

Build Prompt hands the ticket text to the agent in the prompt. The agent has no connection to Freshdesk, so it cannot touch a ticket even if it tried.

## Asking the agent

The agent returns a verdict in tagged fields, not JSON. One malformed field cannot destroy the rest of the answer.

If Check The Answer complains that the disposition is missing, the agent instructions do not match the expected output format. Fix the instructions, not this workflow.

## Filter allowed tags

Any tag not in your allowed_tags list is thrown away here, not written to the ticket. Rejected tags are reported in the note so you can decide whether to add them deliberately.

Tags are **merged** with whatever is already on the ticket. Freshdesk replaces the entire tag array on update, so writing the agent tags alone would silently delete tags a human added.

A Type that is already set is never overwritten.

## Writing back to Freshdesk

Tags are written on every run. Type is written only when the ticket had none. A clean run is silent - no note is added, nothing else on the ticket is touched.

**When the update fails.** Diagnose Failure reads what Freshdesk rejected, the fallback applies the tags on their own, and Explain What Failed posts a private note naming the cause. A tags-only update is the one call that almost always succeeds, so you keep the labels even when Type could not be set.

The usual cause is a **required field that is empty**. Freshdesk revalidates a ticket's required fields on every update and rejects the whole thing if one is blank, without mentioning it in your request. It shows up mostly on tickets that are already closed, where fields required on closure get checked again. Freshly arrived tickets are rarely affected.

If the response is not one this workflow recognises, the note includes the raw error so it can be reported. To stop the notes entirely, disable the **Explain What Failed** node - tags still get applied.
